prior_art_notes: Cassette-format automated DNA size selection: a disposable agarose-filled cassette has electrodes integrated and software-controlled collection wells that elute target size ranges by gating the field at the right time. Anticipates: cassette electrophoresis as a fluidic primitive for NGS / long-read library prep; integration of size-selection into a closed disposable rather than manual gel cut-and-elute. The Pippin cassette is the dominant size-selection step in PacBio HiFi and ONT long-read library prep.
notes: Sage Science was acquired by Felix Biotechnology / Beckman; key consumable for long-read prep.

canonical_name: Diagenode Megaruptor hydrodynamic DNA shearer
disclosure_citation: Diagenode Megaruptor product launch 2013; Megaruptor 3 launch 2019. https://www.diagenode.com/en/p/megaruptor-3.

reproducible fragment sizes
prior_art_notes: Hydrodynamic DNA shearing in a disposable thermoplastic cartridge: a syringe pumps DNA solution through a precisely-defined micro-orifice, the resulting shear forces fragment DNA to a flow-rate-tunable target length. Anticipates: cartridge-based hydrodynamic shearing for long-read library prep, a categorically different fragmentation primitive vs. acoustic (Covaris) or enzymatic (transposase) shearing. Critical consumable for high-quality ONT and PacBio HiFi prep.
notes: The standard hydrodynamic shearer for long-read NGS prep.

canonical_name: Covaris ME220 / E220 focused-ultrasonic DNA shearing
disclosure_citation: Covaris S2 launch 2002; E220 launch ~2010; ME220 launch 2015. https://www.covaris.com/. Laugharn, J. A. et al. Adaptive Focused Acoustics (AFA). US6719449B1.

sample_volume: 10-130 µL per microTUBE

notable_capabilities: isothermal acoustic shearing 100 bp - 5 kb
FFPE-compatible
non-contact (transducer never touches sample)
prior_art_notes: Adaptive Focused Acoustics (AFA): a high-intensity focused-ultrasonic transducer is positioned beneath a glass microTUBE in a degassed water bath; acoustic cavitation in the focal zone shears DNA reproducibly to programmable size. Anticipates: focused-acoustic-cavitation as a non-contact, isothermal DNA-shearing primitive in a disposable glass tube; the architectural pattern of an instrument-side acoustic transducer coupled through a fluid bath to a disposable. The Covaris AFA architecture has been extended to cell lysis, FFPE deparaffinization, and chromatin shearing - a broad prior-art umbrella.
notes: Universal in NGS labs for short-read prep DNA shearing.

canonical_name: Sphere Fluidics Cyto-Mine single-cell screening platform

FACS-style sorting of droplets

Important commercial prior art for the picodroplet cell-line-development workflow.
notes: Closest droplet-based competitor to the Berkeley Lights nanopen architecture.

canonical_name: Berkeley Lights Beacon (PhenomeX, now Bruker) optofluidic platform
disclosure_citation: Berkeley Lights Beacon system launch 2016. Le, K. et al. A novel mammalian cell line development platform utilizing nanofluidics and OptoElectro Positioning technology. prior_art_notes: Optoelectronic-positioning (OEP) single-cell array: a CMOS-photoconductor chip with overlaid microfluidic NanoPen chambers, where projected light patterns generate localized electric-field dielectrophoretic forces that move single cells into individual NanoPens. In-pen assays (proliferation, antibody secretion) are imaged on-instrument; selected clones can be exported. Anticipates: light-addressed dielectrophoretic single-cell handling on a CMOS substrate; the integration of a photoconductor-based DEP positioner with a closed microfluidic NanoPen array for clonal cell-line development; the broader category of light-driven addressable cell-handling chips. Acquisition trajectory (Berkeley Lights -> PhenomeX -> Bruker) and the breadth of the patent family make this a significant prior-art anchor.
notes: Originally Berkeley Lights, rebranded PhenomeX 2022, acquired by Bruker 2023.

canonical_name: Cytena C.SIGHT and B.SIGHT single-cell printers

Foundational to many cell-line development workflows requiring documented monoclonality.
notes: Important predecessor and parallel to Cellenion / WOLF / Namocell single-cell dispensers.

canonical_name: S2 Genomics Singulator tissue dissociation system

Anticipates: cartridge-format upstream sample-prep automation for single-cell genomics, decoupling the upstream dissociation step from the downstream scRNA-seq instrument and reducing operator-dependence. Direct architectural prior art for any 'closed-cartridge tissue-to-suspension automation' claim.
notes: Patent family thin in public databases; draft pending stronger primary IP citation.

canonical_name: Azenta (Brooks) GENEWIZ NGS sample-prep cartridges

linked to GENEWIZ NGS service workflows

Many of these consumables incorporate microfluidic features (e.g. integrated filters in lysis cartridges, sealed transfer ports). Anticipates: the integration of microfluidic-feature-bearing consumables into a sample-management ecosystem rather than a single instrument.
notes: Many consumables are documented only at the catalog level; entry serves to capture the ecosystem rather than a single product.

canonical_name: Hudson Robotics SOLO and PlateMate liquid-handling robots
disclosure_citation: Hudson Robotics PlateMate product line, launched mid-1990s. https://hudsonrobotics.com/. SOLO line for sample-prep automation.
creator: Hudson Robotics

Anticipates: modular workcell-style liquid-handling automation as an alternative to monolithic Hamilton/Tecan workstations; in particular the orchestration-layer-plus-multiple-small-instruments architecture that Opentrons later adopts at much lower cost.
notes: Long-tail mid-tier liquid handler; primary disclosures predominantly catalog material.

canonical_name: Illumina NeoPrep digital-microfluidic NGS library prep

Discontinued 2017 due to library-quality issues, but the disclosed architecture remains useful prior art for any later DMF-based NGS library prep claim. Anticipates: large-cohort DMF library prep on a PCB-substrate EWOD array; the 'cartridge-top + reusable electrode-bottom' architecture for DMF.
notes: Discontinued product, but the disclosure stands as prior art.

canonical_name: ALine integrated multilayer flow cells (laminate microfluidics)
disclosure_citation: ALine Inc. integrated multilayer microfluidic flow cells. https://alineinc.com/. ALine Inc. founded 2002 as a contract designer / manufacturer for laminate-based microfluidic devices.

embedded valves and reagent pouches

Anticipates: PSA-laminate manufacturing as a third major microfluidic fabrication process category alongside soft lithography and thermoplastic injection molding; the architectural pattern of a CRO/CDMO providing both prototyping and production-scale runs of laminate flow cells. Many commercial diagnostic cartridges (including OEM cards inside larger systems) are ALine-built or ALine-architected.
notes: Important contract-manufacturing prior art; many fielded cartridges trace to ALine designs.

canonical_name: Viking 1/2 GCMS and Biology Package
disclosure_citation: Biemann K et al., 'Search for organic and volatile inorganic compounds in two surface samples from the Chryse Planitia region of Mars,' Science 194(4260):72-76 (1976), doi:10.1126/science.194.4260.72; Klein HP, 'The Viking biological investigation: General aspects,' J. Geophys. Res. 82(28):4677-4680 (1977)
creator: NASA / Martin Marietta / MIT (Biemann) / TRW (Biology Instrument)
channel_geometry: Capillary GC column (millimeter-bore packed column to GCMS); biology instrument used three independent ~3 cm^3 incubation cells (Pyrolytic Release, Labeled Release, Gas Exchange) with aliquot transfer plumbing
sample_volume: ~0.1 cm^3 of Mars regolith per analysis cell; 0.5 mL nutrient injection (Labeled Release)
throughput: single-shot per cell; 4-cell magazine for GCMS pyrolyzer
sensing: mass-spec coupled (GCMS); 14C beta detection (Labeled Release); thermal conductivity / GC (Gas Exchange)
notable_capabilities: first in-situ mass spectrometry on a planetary surface
three-way orthogonal life-detection assay (Levin Labeled Release positive at 50 ppb sensitivity)
thermal pyrolysis to 500 C with H2 carrier
operated autonomously for >6 years on the Martian surface
prior_art_notes: Discloses the architectural pattern of a planetary lander instrument that ingests bulk regolith, partitions it across multiple sealed reaction chambers, perfuses each with a different reagent (water/14C-labeled organics/13CO2 + light), and reads out via three orthogonal detection chains (mass spectrometer, beta scintillator, gas chromatograph thermal conductivity). For 102/103 anticipation purposes this is the founding flight precedent for: (a) integrated regolith-to-GCMS pyrolyzer with sealed sample magazines and oven-thermal-cycling, (b) a multi-modal life detection cartridge concept where one physical sample is interrogated by metabolic, isotope-labeling, and gas-evolution assays in parallel, and (c) the use of Curie-point pyrolysis to volatilize organics for downstream chromatographic separation. Anticipates virtually any later 'in-situ astrobiology cartridge' claim that recites multiple parallel reaction wells with independent reagent injection and orthogonal readouts (e.g., contemporary ELSAH/HOLD/MICA concepts). The Labeled Release positive (chiral-asymmetric heat-killable signal) remains a touchstone for any patent claiming life-detection by metabolic 14C release.
sources: Levin GV, Straat PA, 'Recent results from the Viking Labeled Release experiment on Mars,' J. Geophys. Res. 82(28):4663 (1977)
Oyama VI, Berdahl BJ, 'The Viking gas exchange experiment results from Chryse and Utopia surface samples,' J. Geophys. Res. 82:4669 (1977)
Horowitz NH et al., 'The Viking carbon assimilation experiments: Interim report,' Science 194:1321 (1976)
notes: Historic anchor for planetary in-situ chemistry. The four GCMS sample cells in the carousel and the three biology cells together form the canonical multi-modal in-situ astrobiology cartridge, predating MSL/SAM by 36 years.

canonical_name: MSL Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) Wet Chemistry Cell with MTBSTFA Derivatization
aliases: Sample Analysis at Mars Wet Chemistry Experiment
disclosure_citation: Mahaffy PR et al., 'The Sample Analysis at Mars Investigation and Instrument Suite,' Space Science Reviews 170:401-478 (2012), doi:10.1007/s11214-012-9879-z; Glavin DP et al., 'Evidence for perchlorates and the origin of chlorinated hydrocarbons detected by SAM at the Rocknest aeolian deposit in Gale Crater,' JGR Planets 118:1955-1973 (2013)
creator: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / Honeybee Robotics / GSFC SAM team (P. Mahaffy PI)
channel_geometry: 9 sealed metal cups containing MTBSTFA + DMF derivatization reagent and 2 cups containing TMAH for thermochemolysis; foil-pierce actuation; cup interior ~1 cm^3
sample_volume: ~135 mm^3 of pre-sieved (<150 µm) regolith per cup; 1 µL-scale derivatization reagent volumes liberated upon cup heating
throughput: single-use per cup; 9 wet-chemistry derivatization cups + 2 thermochemolysis cups + 59 pyrolysis-only cups in sample carousel
sensing: mass-spec coupled (quadrupole MS, m/z 2-535); 6-column tunable laser spectrometer; gas chromatograph (6 columns)
notable_capabilities: in-situ chemical derivatization of refractory polar organics (amino acids, carboxylic acids) on Mars
perchlorate-tolerant analytical chain via MTBSTFA silylation
first detection of chlorobenzene and dichloroalkanes attributable to indigenous Martian organics (Freissinet 2015)
operates inside SAM oven at >800 C with regolith-to-MS in <2 hours
prior_art_notes: Discloses a sealed reagent-cup architecture for in-situ wet chemistry on a planetary surface: a metal cup with crimped foil seal containing premixed MTBSTFA/DMF derivatization reagent at flight-storage temperature; the cup is mechanically pierced (foil-pierce actuation analogous to terrestrial blister-pack diagnostics), the regolith aliquot is dropped in, and the cup is heated stepwise to release derivatized analytes into the GCMS gas train. For 102/103 anticipation: (a) the foil-pierce + sealed-reagent + thermal-release architecture anticipates any patent claiming a single-use derivatization cartridge for sample-prep before MS, (b) the use of MTBSTFA specifically for in-situ silylation of amino acids/carboxylic acids in the presence of perchlorate oxidizers anticipates Mars/Europa/Enceladus life-detection cartridges that propose perchlorate-tolerant derivatization, and (c) the carousel architecture with mixed wet-chem and pyrolysis-only cups anticipates multi-modal sample-prep cartridges. The post-flight realization that perchlorate combustion was destroying organics during pyrolysis (Glavin 2013) is itself prior art against any claim that perchlorate-mitigation derivatization is novel for astrobiology applications.
sources: Mahaffy PR et al., Space Sci Rev 170:401 (2012)
Glavin DP et al., JGR Planets 118:1955 (2013)
Freissinet C et al., 'Organic molecules in the Sheepbed Mudstone, Gale Crater, Mars,' JGR Planets 120:495-514 (2015)
Eigenbrode JL et al., 'Organic matter preserved in 3-billion-year-old mudstones at Gale crater, Mars,' Science 360:1096 (2018)
notes: SAM is the most-cited in-situ planetary microfluidic instrument in the published literature. The wet-chemistry cup architecture predates Mars 2020 and ExoMars MOMA equivalents.

canonical_name: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin MOMA (Mars Organic Molecule Analyser)
disclosure_citation: Goesmann F et al., 'The Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) Instrument: Characterization of Organic Material in Martian Sediments,' Astrobiology 17(6-7):655-685 (2017), doi:10.1089/ast.2016.1551
creator: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) / NASA GSFC / LISA / CNES / ESA / Thales Alenia Space
channel_geometry: 32-position sample carousel; 20 pyrolysis ovens (single-use), 8 derivatization ovens with MTBSTFA/DMF, 2 thermochemolysis ovens with TMAH; ~250 mg sample per oven; tapping-mode core sampling from 2 m subsurface drill
sample_volume: ~2-30 mg sample subaliquot to GCMS train; ~10-50 µg LDMS spot
throughput: single-use ovens; 32-cell carousel total (different oven types)
sensing: mass-spec coupled (linear ion trap MS, m/z 50-1000); pulsed UV laser desorption ionization (LDI) at 266 nm for refractory aromatics; 4-column GC (3 chiral, 1 polar)
notable_capabilities: combined pyr-GCMS + LDMS in a single MS analyzer (ion-trap)
chiral GC columns for amino-acid enantiomer (D/L) discrimination as biosignature
LDI provides perchlorate-bypassing direct desorption of polyaromatic hydrocarbons
samples drawn from up to 2 m below Martian surface (Rosalind Franklin drill)
prior_art_notes: Discloses a hybrid pyrolysis/derivatization/laser-desorption mass-spec instrument with a 32-cell sealed-cup carousel architecture as in-situ sample prep. Element-by-element disclosure: (a) the dual-front-end design (thermal pyrolysis path + UV-LDI path sharing a single ion trap) anticipates patents claiming dual-mode MS sample introduction for planetary life detection; (b) the chiral-column GC train specifically targeting amino-acid enantiomer ratios as a life-detection signature anticipates terrestrial commercial chiral-LC/GC cartridges marketed for biosignature discrimination; (c) the 2-meter subsurface drill aliquot pathway with sealed transfer to a sample carousel anticipates concepts for Europa Lander / Enceladus subsurface sample acquisition; (d) the perchlorate-bypassing LDI ionization mode anticipates any patent claiming non-thermal direct laser ionization for Mars/icy-moon refractory organics. MOMA is the European/American sister architecture to SAM and the most current public-domain disclosure of an integrated pyr-GCMS-LDMS planetary cartridge.
sources: Vago JL et al., 'Habitability on Early Mars and the Search for Biosignatures with the ExoMars Rover,' Astrobiology 17:471 (2017)
Arevalo R et al., 'Design and demonstration of the Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) on the ExoMars 2018 rover,' IEEE Aerospace Conf. (2015)
Li X et al., 'Mars Organic Molecule Analyzer (MOMA) laser desorption/ionization source design and performance characterization,' Int. J. Mass Spectrom. 422:177 (2017)
notes: Launch slipped from 2018 -> 2022 -> currently 2028 due to ExoMars program reset, but the instrument design and prior art are public-domain since 2017.

canonical_name: Mars 2020 Perseverance SHERLOC (Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman & Luminescence for Organics & Chemicals)
disclosure_citation: Bhartia R et al., 'Perseverance's Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman and Luminescence for Organics and Chemicals (SHERLOC) Investigation,' Space Science Reviews 217:58 (2021), doi:10.1007/s11214-021-00812-z; Beegle LW et al., '2018 SHERLOC instrument briefing'
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory / Photon Systems Inc. (deep-UV laser)
channel_geometry: no fluidic channels per se; arm-mounted instrument addresses a 7x7 mm region with 100 µm laser spot; calibration target carries 5 organic/mineral standards including spacesuit-fabric witness samples
sample_volume: interrogates a ~50 µm spot on rock surface; integrated WATSON microscope provides imaging context
throughput: raster of 1296 points per analysis (~9 hours)
sensing: deep-UV (248.6 nm) Raman and laser-induced fluorescence; resonance Raman cross-section enhancement for aromatics
notable_capabilities: first deep-UV Raman spectrometer on another planet
fluorescence-Raman dual-mode resonance enhancement for aromatic biosignatures (single-molecule sensitivity for PAHs)
calibration target is 5 spacesuit-fabric/Vectran/polycarbonate witnesses for future astronaut-suit material qualification
no sample contact / no sample handling — purely standoff at 48 mm working distance
prior_art_notes: Although SHERLOC has minimal classical fluidics, it is a load-bearing prior art entry for the broader 'in-situ life detection' patent landscape because it discloses (a) a deep-UV resonance-Raman + native-fluorescence dual-mode standoff cartridge architecture as an alternative to wet-chemistry GCMS for organic detection, (b) a co-mounted optical micrometer (WATSON) providing context imaging for spectroscopic point picks, and (c) the use of polymer/fabric witness samples on the calibration target as a vehicle for additional in-flight prior-art disclosure (the spacesuit Vectran/polycarbonate samples become public-domain prior art for astronaut suit polymers by virtue of being launched). For invalidation purposes, SHERLOC anticipates any claim to a deep-UV (sub-260 nm) raster-Raman cartridge for biosignature detection or any claim to a combined Raman/LIF standoff astrobiology head with mineralogical context co-imaging.
sources: Bhartia R et al., Space Sci Rev 217:58 (2021)
Razzell Hollis J et al., 'PIXL and SHERLOC: complementary mineralogy/chemistry instruments,' LPSC 52 (2021)
Beegle LW et al., 'SHERLOC: Scanning Habitable Environments with Raman and Luminescence for Organics and Chemicals, an investigation for 2020,' IEEE Aerospace Conf. (2015)
notes: Paired with PIXL (separate entry) as the Mars 2020 'arm-mounted micro-investigation' duo. SHERLOC's calibration target spacesuit-witness samples are themselves a quietly-important prior art disclosure for astronaut life-support polymer qualification.

canonical_name: Mars 2020 Perseverance PIXL (Planetary Instrument for X-ray Lithochemistry)
disclosure_citation: Allwood AC et al., 'PIXL: Planetary Instrument for X-ray Lithochemistry,' Space Science Reviews 216:134 (2020), doi:10.1007/s11214-020-00767-7
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (A. Allwood PI)
channel_geometry: 120 µm X-ray beam spot; hexapod-positioned scan over ~1 cm^2 areas at ~100 µm steps; helium gas purge of 0.6 L/min through micro-XRF beam path to displace CO2 absorption losses
sample_volume: ~120 µm spot, no sample ingestion (standoff)
throughput: thousands of XRF spectra per scan, ~6-10 hours per map
sensing: micro-X-ray fluorescence (µXRF); 28 mm^2 silicon drift detector; 80-µm-diameter X-ray rhodium-anode source
notable_capabilities: highest spatial resolution elemental imaging on another planet (120 µm)
in-situ helium gas purge of beam path is the principal fluidic subsystem (gas regulator + diffuser at sample face)
co-registered with SHERLOC, WATSON for multi-modal mineral chemistry
operates without sample ingestion or destruction
prior_art_notes: PIXL's microfluidic relevance lies in its low-pressure helium gas purge subsystem and in being the most spatially-resolved astrobiology-grade elemental mapping instrument on another planet. Element-by-element prior art disclosure: (a) gas-purge enclosure of an X-ray beam path on a robotic arm as a workaround for thin-atmosphere absorption losses anticipates patents claiming pressurized-gas-purge atmospheric-isolation envelopes for spectroscopic instruments on planetary rovers, (b) the hexapod 6-DOF micro-positioning system with 50 µm placement repeatability for a microspectroscopy instrument anticipates equivalent industrial precision-fluidic-positioning patents, and (c) PIXL's tight co-registration with SHERLOC's deep-UV map provides prior art for any 'integrated multi-modal arm-mounted astrobiology head' architecture. Co-cite with mars2020-sherloc-spectrometer for the broader Mars 2020 arm-mounted instrument pattern.
sources: Allwood AC et al., Space Sci Rev 216:134 (2020)
Liu Y et al., 'PIXL micro-XRF data processing pipeline,' LPSC 52 (2021)
Tice MM et al., 'Alteration history of Séítah formation rocks inferred by PIXL,' Science Advances 8:eabp9084 (2022)
notes: Included as a fluidic entry primarily for the helium-purge subsystem. The instrument otherwise is X-ray spectroscopy.

canonical_name: Mars 2020 Perseverance MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment)
disclosure_citation: Hecht MH et al., 'Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE),' Space Science Reviews 217:9 (2021), doi:10.1007/s11214-020-00782-8; Hoffman JA et al., 'Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE)—preparing for human Mars exploration,' Science Advances 8:eabp8636 (2022)
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory / MIT Haystack / Niels Bohr Institute / OxEon Energy
channel_geometry: Solid Oxide Electrolysis (SOXE) stack with 10 cells of scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte; 3D-printed superalloy gas-handling manifold; HEPA dust filter; CO2 inlet via scroll compressor at ~1 atm to feed cathode
sample_volume: ingests Mars atmosphere (96% CO2) at ~14 g/hr; produces ~6-10 g O2/hr
throughput: 10+ g O2 per 1-hour run; 16 successful runs across Mars Year 36-37
sensing: mass-flow controllers, electrochemical impedance, in-line oxygen partial pressure sensor
notable_capabilities: first in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) demonstration on another planet
solid-oxide electrochemistry at 800 C in a flight cartridge with scroll compressor pre-stage
feedback-controlled current/voltage operation across day/night Mars atmospheric pressure swings (4-9 mbar)
3D-printed Inconel manifold with integrated channels and getter pre-treatment
ip_citations: US20180023202A1 (NASA application on solid-oxide electrolysis cell stack design — prosecution status varies)
prior_art_notes: Discloses an integrated gas-fluidic cartridge architecture for planetary in-situ resource utilization: (a) scroll-compressor + HEPA particulate filter + 3D-printed superalloy manifold + solid-oxide electrolyzer stack + getter scrubber; (b) the gas-handling subsystem operates as a flow-controlled, feedback-loop system with mass-flow sensors at inlet and oxygen-purity sensors at the anode-side outlet. For 102/103 anticipation: the assembly anticipates patents on integrated planetary atmospheric processing cartridges that combine compression, filtration, electrolysis, and getter purification on a single thermally-managed substrate. The 3D-printed manifold subsystem (additively-manufactured Inconel internal flow paths) is itself prior art against any patent claiming additively-manufactured high-temperature gas-flow manifolds for spaceflight chemical reactors. The stack-level current-voltage feedback control across diurnal pressure variations anticipates closed-loop control patents for variable-input ISRU systems.
sources: Hecht MH et al., Space Sci Rev 217:9 (2021)
Hoffman JA et al., Science Advances 8:eabp8636 (2022)
notes: Patent landscape around solid-oxide cell architecture is dense (OxEon, Ceramatec, Bloom Energy). MOXIE flight is public domain prior art for spaceflight integration.

canonical_name: Phoenix Mars Lander MECA Wet Chemistry Laboratory (WCL)
disclosure_citation: Hecht MH et al., 'Detection of Perchlorate and the Soluble Chemistry of Martian Soil at the Phoenix Lander Site,' Science 325(5936):64-67 (2009), doi:10.1126/science.1172466; Kounaves SP et al., 'The MECA Wet Chemistry Laboratory on the 2007 Phoenix Mars Scout Lander,' JGR Planets 114:E00A19 (2009), doi:10.1029/2008JE003084
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory / Tufts University (Kounaves) / University of Arizona (Hecht PI)
channel_geometry: 4 identical single-use beakers (~25 mL each) with a Teledyne ion-selective electrode array (Li, NH4, Cd, Ca, Mg, Na, K, Cl, NO3, Br, ClO4-equivalent) on the beaker wall; reagent-pellet dispenser releases Li-Mg standard, BaCl2, HNO3 sequentially; magnetic stir-bar agitation
sample_volume: 1 cm^3 of regolith per beaker into 25 mL water solvent + reagent pellets
throughput: single-use, 4 cells total (used 3, 1 retained for contingency)
sensing: ion-selective electrodes (ISEs) for 26 ions; cyclic voltammetry electrode for redox active species; conductivity sensor
notable_capabilities: first wet chemistry analysis of Martian soil-water leachate
discovered perchlorate (ClO4-) at ~0.4-0.6 wt% in Phoenix soils
all-in-one ISE array on a single beaker substrate (sensor wall)
reagent pellets stored dry, dissolved on demand to perform standard additions and titrations
prior_art_notes: Discloses a planetary in-situ wet chemistry cartridge architecture: a sealed disposable reaction beaker with integrated multi-ion electrochemical sensor array on the cell wall, dry-stored reagent pellets released by a mechanical dispenser, and a magnetic stir bar for homogenization. Element-by-element prior art for: (a) any cartridge claim that integrates an ISE array on a single beaker wall with a multi-ion readout (Li, Na, K, NH4, Mg, Ca, Cl, NO3, Br, perchlorate-sensitive); (b) the standard-addition titration protocol implemented through sequential dry-pellet dissolution (the BaCl2 -> SO4 turbidity step, the HNO3 acidification step) anticipates patents on dry-reagent diagnostic cartridges that perform sequential reagent additions for water-quality analysis; (c) the integration of cyclic voltammetry on the same beaker as ion-selective potentiometry anticipates multi-modal electrochemical cartridge designs. The Phoenix WCL is one of two flight precedents (with Viking Biology Instrument) for in-situ aqueous chemistry on a planetary surface.
sources: Kounaves SP et al., JGR Planets 114:E00A19 (2009)
Quinn RC et al., 'Perchlorate radiolysis on Mars and the origin of martian soil reactivity,' Astrobiology 13:515 (2013)
notes: Phoenix WCL is the canonical electrochemical planetary microfluidic prior art. Discovery of perchlorate forced redesign of all subsequent Mars organic-detection cartridges (SAM, MOMA).

canonical_name: ISS Lab-on-Chip Application Development Portable Test System (LOCAD-PTS)
disclosure_citation: Maule J et al., 'Rapid culture-independent microbial analysis aboard the International Space Station (ISS) Stage Two: Quantifying microbial Burden,' Astrobiology 9(8):759-775 (2009), doi:10.1089/ast.2008.0319; Morris HC et al., 'Lab-on-a-Chip Application Development Portable Test System (LOCAD-PTS) on the International Space Station,' SAE Tech. Paper 2007-01-3142 (2007)
creator: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center / Charles River Laboratories (Endosafe-PTS) / University of Surrey
channel_geometry: 4-channel injection-molded cartridge with lyophilized Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) reagent reservoirs and capillary-driven sample inlets; ~25 µL sample per channel; turbidimetric optical readout window
sample_volume: 25 µL per channel x 4 channels = 100 µL total swab eluent
throughput: 1 cartridge per swab in ~15 minutes; LOD ~5 EU/mL endotoxin or equivalent (1->3)-β-D-glucan
sensing: optical (turbidimetric absorbance through cartridge window)
notable_capabilities: first commercial-derivative microfluidic cartridge operated routinely aboard ISS (2006 Expedition 14 onward)
battery-powered handheld with 4-channel parallel LAL chromogenic assay
lyophilized reagents stable in ambient ISS humidity for >18 months
swab-to-result for surface microbial burden in microgravity
prior_art_notes: LOCAD-PTS is the spaceflight derivative of the Charles River Endosafe PTS handheld endotoxin tester. Microfluidic prior art disclosed: (a) the 4-channel parallel capillary-driven cartridge with lyophilized LAL/glucan-detection reagents and integrated optical absorbance window is itself prior art for any cartridge claiming similar handheld bioburden / pyrogen testing in resource-constrained environments (spaceflight, military forward operating, deep-sea); (b) the qualification of the cartridge for microgravity operation (no syringe / no positive pressure source — purely capillary wicking) is prior art for capillary-driven point-of-care cartridges that are deliberately pump-free for environments where pumping is failure-prone; (c) the published ISS protocol for swab-elute-load-read in <15 min anticipates cartridge-based environmental microbial monitoring patents for industrial and built-environment applications. The Charles River Endosafe US patents are the IP citations; the spaceflight qualification is open-published.
sources: Morris HC et al., SAE Tech Paper 2007-01-3142
Endosafe-PTS product literature, Charles River Labs
notes: Operationally important: routine ISS use established spaceflight reliability of capillary-driven thermoplastic cartridges with lyophilized reagents.

canonical_name: ISS WetLab-2 Real-Time RT-PCR on Station
disclosure_citation: Parra M et al., 'Microgravity validation of a novel system for RNA isolation and multiplex quantitative real time PCR analysis of gene expression on the International Space Station,' PLOS ONE 12(9):e0183480 (2017), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0183480; NASA WetLab-2 facility description, ISS Research Office (2016)
creator: NASA Ames Research Center / Cepheid (SmartCycler thermal block heritage) / BioRad (CFX-derived optics)
channel_geometry: 4-tube optical reaction module with integrated Peltier; sample-prep cartridge uses Maxwell-style paramagnetic-bead RNA extraction in a 4-well consumable; transfer pipettes hand-actuated by crew
sample_volume: 10-100 µL extraction; 25 µL RT-qPCR reaction
throughput: 4 reactions in parallel; ~90 min sample-to-Ct
sensing: optical (4-channel real-time fluorescence: FAM, HEX, ROX, Cy5)
notable_capabilities: first qPCR thermal cycling and real-time fluorescence detection performed in microgravity (March 2016)
magnetic-bead RNA extraction validated in microgravity using closed-cartridge / no-pour protocol
consumable cartridge designed for handling without aerosol-generating steps
spaceflight-qualified Peltier thermal cycling at 4-100 C
ip_citations: NASA Ames open-source WetLab-2 protocols (NASA Technical Reports Server)
prior_art_notes: Discloses an end-to-end RNA-extraction + RT-qPCR cartridge architecture qualified for microgravity. Element-by-element prior art: (a) the closed-cartridge magnetic-bead RNA extraction protocol with no open-air liquid transfer steps anticipates patents claiming aerosol-free spaceflight or BSL-3 nucleic acid extraction cartridges; (b) the validation of paramagnetic-bead binding/wash kinetics in zero-G is published prior art against any patent claiming novel microgravity-compatible bead handling; (c) the integration of off-the-shelf SmartCycler-class Peltier modules with a custom reaction tube format anticipates retrofit spaceflight diagnostic cartridge concepts. Combined with iss-biomolecule-sequencer-minion below, WetLab-2 establishes the full sample-prep + amplification + sequencing chain in spaceflight prior art.
sources: Parra M et al., PLOS ONE 12:e0183480 (2017)
Castro-Wallace SL et al., 'Nanopore DNA sequencing and genome assembly on the International Space Station,' Sci. Rep. 7:18022 (2017) (companion paper)
notes: WetLab-2 NASA-released open data positioned this entry as 'open' rather than 'academic'.

canonical_name: ISS Biomolecule Sequencer (Oxford Nanopore MinION on ISS)
disclosure_citation: Castro-Wallace SL et al., 'Nanopore DNA Sequencing and Genome Assembly on the International Space Station,' Scientific Reports 7:18022 (2017), doi:10.1038/s41598-017-18364-0; NASA ISS Biomolecule Sequencer mission press kit, August 2016
creator: NASA Johnson Space Center / Oxford Nanopore Technologies / Houston Methodist
channel_geometry: MinION R7.3/R9 flow cell: 512 channels addressing protein nanopores embedded in a synthetic membrane spanning ~100-µm wells; ASIC reads ionic current through each pore at 4 kHz
sample_volume: 75 µL library load; 1.5 mL of buffer in flow cell reservoir
throughput: up to 30 Gb per flow cell on the ground; ~80 Mb in initial ISS demonstration limited by run time
sensing: ionic current (impedance-derived, ASIC-based picoampere sensing per channel)
notable_capabilities: first DNA sequencing performed in space (August 2016, Kate Rubins)
nanopore protein-membrane chemistry survives launch loads and orbital radiation environment
USB-powered, palm-sized — qualified the architecture for long-duration crewed missions and planetary lander science
real-time basecalling validated in microgravity
prior_art_notes: While the underlying MinION is already covered as 'oxford-nanopore-minion' in the corpus, the spaceflight variant is independent prior art for: (a) the qualification of biological-membrane nanopore arrays for the orbital radiation environment without measurable loss of yield (vs. ground controls), which anticipates patents claiming radiation-hardened or space-qualified single-molecule sequencing cartridges; (b) the ground-to-orbit cold-chain protocol for shipping pre-loaded R9 flow cells (cold pack stability, ambient ISS temperature operation), which anticipates patents on planetary or deep-sea biosensor logistics; (c) the integration of MinION sequencing with WetLab-2 sample prep on station — together these establish the first sample-to-sequence loop performed beyond Earth, and anticipate any patent claim to an integrated 'in-situ sequencing cartridge' for planetary life detection that uses pore-based single-molecule readout. Cross-cite to oxford-nanopore-minion for the underlying device.
sources: Castro-Wallace SL et al., Sci Rep 7:18022 (2017)
John JG et al., 'Genes in Space-3: Identifying microbes on the ISS via PCR + nanopore sequencing,' iScience (2018)
NASA ISS Biomolecule Sequencer press kit Aug 2016
notes: Cross-references oxford-nanopore-minion (entry 118) for the underlying device. This entry covers the spaceflight-specific qualification disclosure.

canonical_name: Europa Clipper SUrface Dust mass Analyzer (SUDA)
disclosure_citation: Kempf S et al., 'SUrface Dust Analyzer (SUDA): An impact ionization mass spectrometer for compositional mapping of Europa,' Space Science Reviews 220:31 (2024), doi:10.1007/s11214-024-01057-2
creator: Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP) / University of Colorado Boulder / NASA JPL / DLR
channel_geometry: Time-of-flight mass spectrometer (~1 m drift tube) with ~220 cm^2 impact target plate; particles >0.2 µm hypervelocity-ionize on the target generating cation plume; m/Δm ~200-400 across m/z 1-1000
sample_volume: ingests dust particles ejected from Europa's surface during flybys; ~10^-15 g per impact
throughput: ~10^4 particle spectra per Europa flyby (estimate)
sensing: mass-spec coupled (impact ionization time-of-flight)
notable_capabilities: compositional mapping of icy-moon surfaces by impact-ionization MS during flyby
no liquid sample handling — particle-in, m/z-out
can detect amino acids, salts, organics in the impact plume
heritage from Cassini Cosmic Dust Analyzer (CDA) and Stardust
prior_art_notes: Discloses a particle-impact ionization mass spectrometer designed for in-flight compositional analysis of icy moon dust ejecta. Microfluidic-adjacent prior art: (a) the impact-target + acceleration-grid + ToF-drift architecture is independent prior art for impact-ionization sample introduction patents (alternative to electrospray, MALDI, etc.); (b) the disclosed particle-detection rate and mass resolution requirements for amino acid identification in icy-moon plumes anticipate any patent claiming an instrument architecture for biosignature detection in Enceladus/Europa plume material; (c) the calibration database for ice-mineral-organic mixtures (LASP impact testing) is open prior art for spectral interpretation algorithms in impact-ionization MS. Co-cite with cassini-cda-cosmic-dust-analyzer.
sources: Kempf S et al., Space Sci Rev 220:31 (2024)
Kempf S et al., 'Compositional mapping of Europa using dynamic SUDA,' EPSC2018-XXX (2018)
notes: Heritage line: Stardust CIDA -> Cassini CDA -> Europa Clipper SUDA. Co-cite with cassini-cda entry below.

canonical_name: Cassini Cosmic Dust Analyzer (CDA) — Enceladus Plume Mass Spectra
disclosure_citation: Srama R et al., 'The Cassini Cosmic Dust Analyzer,' Space Science Reviews 114:465-518 (2004), doi:10.1007/s11214-004-1435-z; Postberg F et al., 'Macromolecular organic compounds from the depths of Enceladus,' Nature 558:564-568 (2018), doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0246-4
creator: Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics (MPI-K Heidelberg) / NASA / ESA Cassini-Huygens
channel_geometry: 0.41 m^2 collection target with central 17 cm Chemical Analyzer Subsystem (CAT) for impact ionization; ToF flight tube; ~1 m^2 effective sensing area total
sample_volume: captures hypervelocity ice/dust grains ejected from Enceladus plume; ~10^-15 to 10^-12 g per particle
throughput: thousands of grain impact spectra over Enceladus flybys (E2-E22)
sensing: mass-spec coupled (impact-ionization ToF, CAT subsystem); impact charge subsystem (current pulse on target)
notable_capabilities: confirmed liquid water ocean inside Enceladus via salt detection in plume ice grains (Postberg 2009)
detected complex macromolecular organics (>200 u) in Enceladus plume material (Postberg 2018)
heritage for all subsequent icy-moon dust mass spectrometers (SUDA, ENIJA)
prior_art_notes: Founding flight precedent for in-situ icy-moon plume composition analysis. Element-by-element prior art for: (a) hypervelocity impact + plasma plume + ToF-MS for compositional analysis of micron-scale ice grains in flyby geometry; (b) the dual-mode operation (charge-pulse for particle counting + mass spectrum for composition) on a single sensing area; (c) the post-mission discovery that Enceladus plume material contains complex organics and salts is itself open prior art that any future Enceladus mission cartridge claiming biosignature detection will need to overcome. CDA is the citation grandparent for all icy-moon life-detection cartridges.
sources: Srama R et al., Space Sci Rev 114:465 (2004)
Khawaja N et al., 'Low-mass nitrogen-, oxygen-bearing, and aromatic compounds in Enceladean ice grains,' MNRAS 489:5231 (2019)
notes: Cassini operated 2004-2017. Postberg 2018 detection of macromolecular organics in plume grains is the strongest open prior art for any astrobiology cartridge designed to interrogate Enceladus material.

canonical_name: Dragonfly Mass Spectrometer (DraMS) for Titan
disclosure_citation: Trainer MG et al., 'Dragonfly: Investigating the Surface Composition of Titan,' Planetary Science Journal 3:218 (2022), doi:10.3847/PSJ/ac8e9d; Grubisic A et al., 'DraMS: Architecture and capabilities of the Dragonfly Mass Spectrometer,' International Astronautical Congress IAC-22 (2022)
creator: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / Johns Hopkins APL / DraMS team (M. Trainer PI)
channel_geometry: Linear ion trap MS (m/z 10-1000+); dual front end: pyrolysis ovens with sample carousel + UV laser desorption ionization (LDI) at 266 nm; designed to drink directly from drilled Titan surface samples acquired by DrACO sampler
sample_volume: ~10 mg per pyrolysis oven; ~50 µg per LDI spot
throughput: few-dozen analyses per Titan year (limited by drill sample availability)
sensing: mass-spec coupled (linear ion trap, MOMA-derived heritage)
notable_capabilities: MOMA-class linear ion trap optimized for Titan cryogenic surface chemistry
dual pyrolysis + UV-LDI front end as in MOMA but tuned for nitrile-rich Titan tholins
drill-coupled (DrACO) sample acquisition from drone-deployed lander platform
operates at Titan ambient (-179 C) with thermal subsystem for the MS analyzer at room T
prior_art_notes: Discloses the MOMA-derivative architecture adapted for Titan operation. Element-by-element prior art: (a) the cryogenic-surface-to-MS sample handling chain (DrACO drill -> sealed cryotransfer -> warmed pyrolysis oven -> ion trap MS) anticipates patents on cryogenic-sample mass-spec sample-introduction cartridges; (b) the pulse-frequency tuning of the 266 nm UV-LDI source for nitrile/tholin chemistry anticipates LDI-MS patents claiming optimized parameters for nitrogen-rich complex organics; (c) the integration of MS with a flying lander (drone) platform, including vibration-tolerance qualification of the linear ion trap, anticipates patents on platform-integrated mass spectrometers for non-rover planetary missions. Co-cite with exomars-moma-pyr-gcms-ldms for the heritage instrument.
sources: Grubisic A et al., IAC-22 paper (2022)
Lorenz RD et al., 'Dragonfly: A rotorcraft lander concept for scientific exploration at Titan,' Johns Hopkins APL Tech Digest 34:374 (2018)
notes: Launch NET 2028, Titan arrival ~2034. Disclosure dates from 2022 instrument architecture publications.

canonical_name: OSIRIS-REx TAGSAM (Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism)
disclosure_citation: Bierhaus EB et al., 'The OSIRIS-REx Spacecraft and the Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism (TAGSAM),' Space Science Reviews 214:107 (2018), doi:10.1007/s11214-018-0521-6; Lauretta DS et al., 'Asteroid (101955) Bennu in the laboratory: Properties of the sample collected by OSIRIS-REx,' Meteoritics & Planetary Science 59:2453 (2024)
creator: Lockheed Martin Space / NASA Goddard / University of Arizona (D. Lauretta PI)
channel_geometry: Sample head: ~30 cm diameter chamber with annular nitrogen gas-purge ports that fluidize regolith into the collector during a ~5 second touch-and-go contact; Velcro-pad surface contact pads on the bottom; sealed with O-ring on retraction
sample_volume: design target 60 g / minimum success 60 g / actual collected 121.6 g of Bennu regolith
throughput: single-event sample acquisition
sensing: mass-on-arm via spacecraft inertial properties; visible/IR imaging during contact
notable_capabilities: nitrogen-jet-fluidized regolith capture mechanism (active gas-purge sampling)
first US asteroid sample return mission; sample arrived Sept 2023
demonstrated controlled-atmosphere capture of friable carbonaceous chondrite material
TAGSAM head canister enables nominal 1 atm N2 storage of pristine sample for return
prior_art_notes: The TAGSAM head is a gas-fluidized sample acquisition cartridge — relevant to the microfluidics corpus as a non-canonical fluidic system: pressurized N2 jets fluidize asteroid regolith into the collection chamber, then the chamber is sealed with an O-ring against contamination. Element-by-element prior art for: (a) gas-fluidized loose-particulate sampling cartridges with sealed return architecture (anticipates terrestrial industrial fluid-bed dry-sample collectors and bio-aerosol capture cartridges); (b) the integration of multiple sample-capture methods on one head (gas jets + Velcro contact pads) anticipates patents claiming hybrid dry-sampling cartridges; (c) the curation chain from in-flight sealed canister -> Earth-return capsule -> JSC nitrogen glove-box curation establishes a published cleanroom protocol for friable carbonaceous samples that anticipates Mars Sample Return curation patents. Patent citation is for the Lockheed-developed sample capture architecture.
sources: Bierhaus EB et al., Space Sci Rev 214:107 (2018)
Lauretta DS et al., 'OSIRIS-REx asteroid sample collection: Decadal-class achievement,' AGU 2023 abstracts
notes: Bennu sample showed evidence of phyllosilicates, organics including amino acids and nucleobases. The disclosed gas-fluidization fluidic mechanism is the relevant microfluidics-corpus content.

canonical_name: MBARI Environmental Sample Processor (ESP)
disclosure_citation: Scholin CA et al., 'The Environmental Sample Processor (ESP) — An autonomous robotic device for detecting microorganisms remotely using molecular probe technology,' Proc. OCEANS 2003: 1-7 (2003); Scholin CA et al., 'Remote detection of marine microbes, small invertebrates, harmful algae, and biotoxins using the Environmental Sample Processor (ESP),' Oceanography 22(2):158-167 (2009)
creator: Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) (Scholin lab) / McLane Research Laboratories (commercial 2G/3G ESP)
channel_geometry: Carousel of ~100 single-use 'pucks' with on-board filter, lysis chamber, and reagent reservoirs; integrated peristaltic pumps and rotary multiport valves; 1-2 L sample volume filtered per puck
sample_volume: 1-2 L seawater filtered onto 25 mm filter per puck; 200-500 µL reagent volumes downstream
throughput: ~50-100 pucks per 6-12 month deployment; one assay per puck (sandwich hybridization or ddPCR)
sensing: optical (chemiluminescence, fluorescence); some 3G ESPs include in-line ddPCR (qPCR variant)
notable_capabilities: fully autonomous in-situ molecular biology lab on a moored buoy or AUV (LRAUV)
sandwich hybridization assay for harmful algal bloom species and toxin detection
later 3G-ESP integrated with Long-Range AUV for adaptive plume sampling
single deployment can run for 6+ months without intervention
prior_art_notes: The ESP is the canonical autonomous oceanographic microfluidic robotic sampler. Element-by-element prior art for: (a) automated puck-carousel architecture with integrated filtration + lysis + sandwich-hybridization assay + chemiluminescent readout in a long-deployment marine-robotic platform; (b) feedback-controlled adaptive sampling where the on-board assay result triggers subsequent sample collection (LRAUV+ESP plume tracking); (c) integration of ddPCR into a marine autonomous vehicle (3G ESP), which anticipates patents on autonomous in-situ qPCR/ddPCR cartridges for environmental monitoring; (d) the sealed puck format with pre-loaded dry/wet reagents stored at ocean depth for months anticipates patents on long-storage diagnostic cartridges in extreme environments. ESP is also the closest terrestrial analog to a planetary in-situ life detection cartridge.
sources: Scholin CA et al., OCEANS 2003 proceedings
Pargett DM et al., 'Long-term autonomous monitoring of bacterial communities by an Environmental Sample Processor,' Microbial Ecology 73:813 (2017)
Yamahara KM et al., 'In situ autonomous acquisition and preservation of marine environmental DNA using an autonomous underwater vehicle,' Front. Mar. Sci. 6:373 (2019)
notes: Most-deployed autonomous in-situ molecular cartridge platform on Earth; cited heavily by all subsequent autonomous environmental DNA / harmful algal bloom monitoring cartridges.

canonical_name: WISSARD / SALSA Subglacial Antarctic Microbial Samplers
disclosure_citation: Christner BC et al., 'A microbial ecosystem beneath the West Antarctic ice sheet,' Nature 512:310-313 (2014), doi:10.1038/nature13667; Priscu JC et al., 'Scientific access into Mercer Subglacial Lake: scientific objectives, drilling operations and initial observations,' Annals of Glaciology 62:340-352 (2021)
creator: WISSARD project (Whillans Ice Stream Subglacial Access Research Drilling) / SALSA project (Subglacial Antarctic Lakes Scientific Access) / NSF funded multi-institution
channel_geometry: Niskin-style sampler bottles modified for microbial cleanliness (Trebesch closures with silane-treated interiors); on-deck filtration through 0.2 µm Sterivex cartridges; on-site DNA extraction in clean tents using closed-cartridge MoBio PowerWater extraction
sample_volume: 10 L water samples filtered onto Sterivex membranes; subsequent 10 mL elution per cartridge for downstream sequencing
throughput: ~20 sample bottles per drill access event
sensing: optical (epifluorescence DAPI counts on-site); off-site Illumina/PacBio sequencing
notable_capabilities: first uncontaminated retrieval of liquid water from a subglacial Antarctic lake (Lake Whillans 2013, Lake Mercer 2018)
hot-water drill with HEPA-filtered + UV-sterilized drill water to maintain <10^3 cells/mL drill-water bioburden
Sterivex closed-cartridge filter format adopted as the de facto standard for clean subglacial sampling
directly analogous to proposed Europa/Enceladus subsurface ocean sampling protocols
prior_art_notes: Discloses the cleanest-published terrestrial protocol for retrieving microbiologically-pristine subsurface aqueous samples — the most directly cited prior art for any future Europa/Enceladus subsurface life detection mission. Element-by-element: (a) hot-water drill with multi-stage HEPA + 0.2 µm filtration + UV-C sterilization of drill water anticipates patents claiming planetary subsurface drilling fluid sterilization architectures; (b) Sterivex closed-cartridge format with sealed inlet/outlet for downstream nucleic acid extraction without breaking sterility anticipates planetary sample-handling cartridges that must preserve sterility from sample-take through analysis; (c) the published clean-tent protocols and contamination-control budgets are open prior art that any 'planetary protection' patent would have to overcome. WISSARD/SALSA are the gold standard for terrestrial-analog subsurface-ocean sampling.
sources: Priscu JC et al., Annals of Glaciology 62:340 (2021)
Mikucki JA et al., 'Subglacial Lake Whillans microbial biogeochemistry: a synthesis of current knowledge,' Phil. Trans. Royal Soc. A 374:20140290 (2016)
Davis CL et al., 'Microbial dynamics in a subglacial lake during melt season,' Limnology and Oceanography 68:S26 (2023)
notes: Direct terrestrial analog for Europa/Enceladus mission planning. WISSARD also pre-dates the more famous Subglacial Lake Vostok (Lake Vostok work was contamination-compromised and cannot be cited as clean prior art).

canonical_name: Mathies/Quinn 2017 Microchip Capillary Electrophoresis for Mars Amino Acid Detection
disclosure_citation: Mora MF et al., 'Toward total automation of microfluidics for extraterrestrial in situ analysis,' Anal. Chem. 83:8636 (2011); Mora MF et al. (Mathies/Quinn group), 'Capillary electrophoresis amino acid sensitivity from a chip-based instrument,' Electrophoresis 38:2982 (2017), doi:10.1002/elps.201700110
creator: Richard Mathies group (UC Berkeley) / Peter Willis (NASA JPL) / Maria Mora (NASA JPL) / Aaron Noell
channel_geometry: Glass microchip CE separation channel ~25 cm; LIF detection downstream; integrated programmable membrane microvalve array (Quake-style PDMS-on-glass) for sample dilution, fluorescent labeling with Pacific Blue or fluorescamine, and injection into the CE channel
sample_volume: ~10 nL injected onto the CE channel from ~10 µL processed sample
throughput: single CE run, 10-20 minutes; ~100 ppt (parts-per-trillion) amino acid LOD
sensing: fluorescence-on-chip (LIF with Pacific Blue / fluorescamine derivatization)
notable_capabilities: first sub-ppb amino acid detection in a flight-prototype microchip CE for Mars/icy moons
integrated programmable PDMS-on-glass valve array for full sample preparation (extraction + labeling + injection) on chip
chiral separation capability for D/L amino acid biosignature detection
directly proposed as instrument payload for ELSAH (Enceladus Life Signatures and Habitability) and other concept missions
prior_art_notes: The Mathies/Quinn line of work is the most extensively-published academic flight-prototype for microfluidic life detection on Mars and icy moons. Element-by-element prior art: (a) the integration of programmable PDMS-on-glass membrane valves with on-chip CE separation for extraterrestrial sample analysis anticipates any patent claiming integrated sample-prep + electrophoretic-separation + LIF cartridges for planetary instruments; (b) the published parts-per-trillion sensitivity for fluorescamine-labeled amino acids in a portable / battery-powered instrument anticipates patents claiming similar sensitivity in handheld biosensors; (c) chiral separation as a biosignature-discrimination strategy on a microchip CE format anticipates any patent claiming D/L enantiomer microfluidic separation for biosignature detection. The Mora 2011/2017 papers also disclose the architectural pattern of a fully-automated 'Mars Organic Analyzer' (MOA) cartridge.
sources: Mora MF et al., Anal Chem 83:8636 (2011)

Skelley AM, Mathies RA, 'Chiral separation of fluorescamine-labeled amino acids using microfabricated capillary electrophoresis devices for extraterrestrial exploration,' J. Chromatogr. A 1021:191 (2003)
Willis PA et al., 'Investigation of microfluidic sample preparation for the SOLID life-detection instrument,' LPSC 41 (2010)
notes: Lineage ancestor: skelley-2009-cell-pairing-trap (separate Mathies-group entry); also cited as the prior art for any future Enceladus/Mars amino acid microfluidic cartridge.

canonical_name: Dexcom G6 Continuous Glucose Monitor
disclosure_citation: FDA 510(k) clearance DEN170088 (Dexcom G6, March 27 2018); Dexcom press release March 27 2018; US patent 9,724,025 (in vivo glucose sensor)
creator: Dexcom Inc.
notable_capabilities: 10-day continuous wear
no fingerstick calibration
factory-calibrated glucose oxidase enzyme amperometry
subcutaneous filament 0.4mm diameter delivering interstitial fluid sampling at the working electrode
prior_art_notes: Discloses a wearable CGM in which a thin polymer-membrane-coated platinum filament is inserted subcutaneously by a single-use applicator and continuously samples interstitial fluid via passive diffusion across an outer biocompatible polymer (the diffusion-limiting membrane). The membrane stack creates a microliter-scale sample envelope at the electrode surface where glucose oxidase generates hydrogen peroxide that is amperometrically quantified. Anticipates: factory-calibrated subcutaneous glucose sensors with diffusion-limited polymer envelopes; single-button push insertion of a microneedle-style sensor with auto-retraction; transmitter-on-patch architectures using BLE telemetry. Element-by-element it teaches every subsystem now considered standard for CGMs except the redox mediator chemistry choice.
sources: Christiansen et al. Diabetes Technol Ther 20(6) 2018 doi:10.1089/dia.2018.0067

canonical_name: Dexcom G5 Mobile Continuous Glucose Monitor
disclosure_citation: FDA PMA P120005/S041 supplement August 2015; Dexcom press release 2015-08-24
creator: Dexcom Inc.
notable_capabilities: 7-day wear
first FDA-approved smartphone-direct CGM (Bluetooth to iPhone)
two-fingerstick-per-day calibration
prior_art_notes: Predecessor to G6 (already in corpus). Discloses subcutaneous platinum filament with multilayer polymer envelope (interferent-blocking layer / glucose-oxidase enzyme layer / diffusion-limiting outer polymer). Anticipates: smartphone-tethered CGM data architectures and the multilayer membrane chemistry approach used across modern CGMs.

non-prescription glucose tracking for non-insulin-using adults

5-day wear

canonical_name: Senseonics Eversense Implantable Continuous Glucose Monitor
disclosure_citation: CE-Mark 2016; FDA PMA P160048 June 2018; Senseonics 10-K filings
creator: Senseonics Holdings Inc.
notable_capabilities: fully implantable subcutaneous sensor (90 to 365-day wear depending on generation)
fluorescence-based boronic-acid glucose recognition (not enzymatic)
external transmitter optically powers and reads the implanted polymer hydrogel

canonical_name: Halo MJOLNIR armor biofoam emergency wound-sealant injector
disclosure_citation: Halo: Combat Evolved (Bungie/Microsoft, 2001); detailed in Halo: The Fall of Reach (Eric Nylund, Del Rey ISBN 978-0-345-45132-3, 2001) and Halo: First Strike (Eric Nylund, 2003).

prior_art_notes: Discloses an armor-integrated wound-sealant fluidic dispenser. The combat-armor automated injector concept is repeatedly described across Halo novels and games 2001-present and is depicted as a hands-free wearable microfluidic-equivalent sealant dispenser. Defensive prior art for hands-free combat-medic auto-injectors, wearable hemostatic foam dispensers, and biosensor-triggered drug delivery integrated into clothing/armor.

prior_art_notes: Detailed multi-stage biological augmentation pipeline: candidates undergo coordinated injections of carbide-ceramic ossification compound (skeletal infusion), muscular-density growth catalysts, occipital-capillary reversal protein, superconducting fibrification of neural dendrites, and catalytic thyroid implants. Architecturally anticipates a programmable multi-reagent timed-injection regimen administered through a single integrated patient-bed pumping system; couples diagnostic monitoring with sequenced infusion. The ~3:1 mortality figure (33 of 75 candidates surviving) makes the Project ORION protocol one of the most detailed fictional descriptions of an automated multi-channel infusion bed. Defensive prior art for: programmed multi-channel infusion stations, integrated patient-bed perfusion + monitoring loops, and time-resolved augmentation drug regimens.

prior_art_notes: Iconic and one of the most detailed fictional biological-compiler systems in SF. The 1976-1985 publication window predates virtually all modern bioreactor tissue-engineering patents.

The Heinzl-Hertz comprehensive 1985 review is also foundational prior art for the field. Important for distinguishing Hertz CIJ from Sweet CIJ in priority disputes.

prior_art_notes: Caltech/Quake monolithic-membrane valve patent family. Anchors claims around: (a) two-layer PDMS device in which a flow channel is occluded by deflection of a thin elastomeric membrane via pressurization of an orthogonal control channel; (b) push-down geometry where the control channel sits above the flow channel; (c) push-up geometry where the control channel sits below; (d) integration of large arrays of such valves on a single monolithic device (microfluidic large-scale integration); (e) peristaltic pump architectures using three valves in series; (f) multiplexer trees that address N flow lines with log2(N) control lines. These claims are the licensing root that Fluidigm built its IFC controller, BioMark dynamic array, Access Array, C1 single-cell, and Helios CyTOF business on. Anticipates virtually any PDMS multilayer monolithic valve device unless distinguished by materials (non-PDMS), actuation (non-pneumatic), or geometry (non-membrane closure). canonical_name: Mayo Collaborative Services v. Prometheus Laboratories 2012 (Diagnostic-Method Patentability)
creator: Supreme Court of the United States
notable_capabilities: narrowed Section 101 patent eligibility for diagnostic methods

prior_art_notes: Case-law entry. Mayo v. Prometheus 566 U.S. 66 (2012) narrowed 35 USC Section 101 patent eligibility for diagnostic methods, holding that a claim reciting a natural correlation (here, between thiopurine metabolite levels and dosing) plus conventional measurement steps is not patent-eligible subject matter. Direct relevance to microfluidics: any cartridge-or-method patent that claims merely 'measure analyte X with my cartridge and infer condition Y' is at risk under Mayo. Combined with Myriad (gene patents) and Alice (software-implemented), forms the modern Section 101 trilogy. Defensive value: any microfluidic cartridge patent practitioner should evaluate Section 101 risk under Mayo before relying on broad diagnostic-correlation claims.
notes: Foundational case-law entry. 102/103 prior art is the wrong frame for case law; this entry is an enforceability-defense reference rather than novelty prior art. Categorized as `corpus: academic` (public-domain status captured in `ip_status`).

Combined with Mayo and Myriad, defines modern Section 101 limitations.

canonical_name: Stone & Kim 2001 — Microfluidics: basic issues, applications, and challenges
creator: Howard A. Stone, Sam Kim
prior_art_notes: Editorial-review framing of the nascent microfluidics field at the chemical-engineering scale. Discloses the canonical taxonomy of microfluidic challenges (low Reynolds, diffusion-limited mixing, surface-tension dominance, manufacturability constraints, integration with off-chip macroworld) before any 'microfluidics platform' patents on those general architectures issued. Anticipates: claims that abstract over a 'microfluidic platform comprising channels of <500 µm characteristic dimension exploiting laminar flow, surface tension, and capillarity for chemical or biological assay' — i.e., genus-level claims naming low-Re flow as the operative principle. Establishes the engineering-principles framing that a competent examiner uses to reject overly broad microfluidic genus claims as obvious in view of a published research agenda.

canonical_name: Beebe, Mensing & Walker 2002 — Physics and applications of microfluidics in biology

prior_art_notes: Comprehensive Annual Reviews chapter cataloguing the physics governing microfluidics for biology: laminar flow, diffusional mixing, electrokinetic phenomena, capillarity, two-phase flow, and surface chemistry; with applied examples in cell handling, immunoassays, PCR, and DNA analysis. Specifically anticipates 'soft-lithography PDMS device for cell-based assay' and 'electroosmotically driven biochemical analysis' as obvious combinations.
