creator: Andreas Manz, Holger Becker (RSC)
prior_art_notes: Inaugural editorial of the Royal Society of Chemistry's Lab on a Chip journal, by the originators of the µTAS concept. Functions as a published roadmap document declaring the field's scope: integrated chemical and biological analysis on planar substrates using microfabricated channels, valves, mixers, separators, and detectors. By 2001 disclosure-genus, this editorial is citable to defeat any later attempt to patent 'an integrated lab-on-chip system' as a novel concept. Critically, it establishes the journal of record whose archive then continuously time-stamps disclosures of every subsequent micro-platform.
sources: Lab on a Chip volume 1 issue 1

canonical_name: Auroux, Iossifidis, Reyes & Manz 2002 — Micro total analysis systems part 2 (analytical standard operations and applications)
creator: Pierre-Alain Auroux, Dimitri Iossifidis, Darwin R. Reyes, Andreas Manz
prior_art_notes: Companion review to Reyes 2002 (already in the corpus); covers analytical standard operations on chip — sample injection, mixing, reaction, separation, and detection. Catalogues by 2002 the entire 'unit operations on chip' library: pneumatic and thermal valving, electrokinetic injection, T- and Y-mixers, electrophoretic separation, optical and electrochemical detection. Anticipates: any patent that combines two or more of these unit operations into an 'integrated microfluidic system' — the combinatorial space was already published. Specifically defeats novelty for 'on-chip injector + separator + detector' genus claims after 2002.

canonical_name: Mark, Haeberle, Roth, von Stetten & Zengerle 2010 — Microfluidic lab-on-a-chip platforms
creator: Daniel Mark, Stefan Haeberle, Günter Roth, Felix von Stetten, Roland Zengerle
prior_art_notes: Critical Chem Soc Rev cataloguing the seven dominant microfluidic platforms by 2010: capillary, pressure-driven, centrifugal, electrokinetic, acoustic, free-flow, and droplet/digital. For each it lists fabrication, fluidic operations achievable, and example applications — i.e., a public engineering manual. Anticipates: any post-2010 patent that claims a 'microfluidic platform' architecturally indistinguishable from one of these seven (e.g., 'a centrifugal disc with siphon valves and detection chamber') as obvious in view of the Mark 2010 enumeration. Particularly load-bearing for centrifugal and droplet platform genus claims.

canonical_name: Whitesides 2014 — Cool, or simple and cheap? Why not both?
disclosure_citation: doi:10.1039/C4LC90072C; Lab Chip 13, 11-13 (2013) editorial; reprinted Lab Chip 14, 3125 (2014)
creator: George M. Whitesides
prior_art_notes: Editorial articulating the design imperative for low-cost, frugal microfluidic platforms (paper, thread, scotch-tape, capillary) targeted at global health and resource-limited settings. Disclosure timestamps the design space of 'simple, cheap, no-instrument' microfluidic devices as a published research program. Anticipates: any later patent on a 'lateral-flow-like microfluidic device fabricated from cellulose or thread for diagnostic use' as obvious; reinforces the µPAD prior art commons.

canonical_name: Convery & Gadegaard 2019 — 30 years of microfluidics
disclosure_citation: doi:10.1016/j.mne.2019.01.003; Micro and Nano Engineering 2, 76-91 (2019)
creator: Neil Convery, Nikolaj Gadegaard
prior_art_notes: Retrospective that catalogues the 30-year arc from Manz 1990 µTAS to 2019 commercial platforms, with explicit lineage maps for soft-lithography, droplet, digital-microfluidics, organ-on-chip, and paper platforms. By aggregating prior disclosures into a single citable archive, this paper is itself useful as a chain-of-custody document for invalidity contentions: it ties together the publication dates of foundational disclosures so that an examiner can reject 'X on a chip' claims as obvious combinations of pre-existing known elements.

canonical_name: Tabeling 2005 — Introduction to Microfluidics (textbook)
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-0198568643; Oxford University Press, 2005
creator: Patrick Tabeling
prior_art_notes: Foundational graduate textbook by ESPCI's Patrick Tabeling. Systematically covers low-Re hydrodynamics, diffusion, capillarity, electrokinetics, two-phase flow, and surface chemistry as applied to microfluidic devices; with worked engineering examples. As a textbook, the engineering descriptions of the underlying physics and unit operations are unencumbered prior art (copyright attaches only to the specific text). Anticipates: any patent claim that recites a generic microfluidic device whose operation is governed by one of the textbook's worked physics — particularly electroosmotic flow, capillary filling, droplet generation by flow focusing, and pressure-driven Hagen-Poiseuille flow at micron scale. A standard examiner reference.

canonical_name: Bruus 2008 — Theoretical Microfluidics (textbook)
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-0199235094; Oxford University Press, 2008
creator: Henrik Bruus
prior_art_notes: Definitive theoretical textbook covering the full Navier-Stokes/electrokinetic/acoustofluidic framework for microfluidic devices, with closed-form analytical solutions and dimensionless-number scaling. Includes complete derivations of: Hagen-Poiseuille flow in arbitrary cross-sections, Stokes drag, electroosmotic flow with EDL, capillary filling, acoustic radiation forces, and dielectrophoresis. Anticipates: any patent claim whose only novelty is the application of one of these textbook physics to an obvious microfluidic geometry. Frequently cited in invalidity contentions for 'novel acoustofluidic device' or 'novel electrokinetic separator' claims that merely re-implement textbook physics.

canonical_name: Kirby 2010 — Micro- and Nanoscale Fluid Mechanics: Transport in Microfluidic Devices (textbook)
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-0521119030; Cambridge University Press, 2010
creator: Brian J. Kirby
prior_art_notes: Comprehensive engineering textbook on micro- and nanoscale fluid transport with emphasis on electrokinetics, electroosmosis, electrophoresis, dielectrophoresis, and species transport. Treats Debye layer physics, Smoluchowski slip, zeta-potential measurement, and electrokinetic separations. Anticipates: claims to electrokinetic microfluidic separators, ion-selective nanofluidic devices, and electrophoretic concentration platforms whose operating principle is a textbook derivation. The book's chapter on ion concentration polarization predates many later patents on ICP-based desalination and preconcentration.

canonical_name: Nguyen & Wereley 2006 — Fundamentals and Applications of Microfluidics (2nd ed) (textbook)
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-1580539722; Artech House, 2nd edition, 2006 (1st ed 2002)
creator: Nam-Trung Nguyen, Steven T. Wereley
prior_art_notes: Engineering textbook with extensive device-level coverage: micropumps (electrokinetic, piezo, peristaltic, thermopneumatic, MHD), microvalves (active and passive, check, pinch, ball), micromixers (passive lamination, chaotic advection, active acoustic and electrokinetic), and detection. Each device class is described in enough engineering detail to enable an undergraduate to build it. Anticipates: device-level patent claims on microfluidic pumps, valves, and mixers in any of the listed taxonomies — they are obvious in view of this textbook's catalog. Particularly load-bearing: catalog of 'pump architectures usable on chip' defeats narrow novelty for any post-2002 micropump claim.

canonical_name: Karniadakis, Beskok & Aluru 2005 — Microflows and Nanoflows: Fundamentals and Simulation (textbook)
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-0387221977; Springer Interdisciplinary Applied Mathematics vol 29, 2005
creator: George Em Karniadakis, Ali Beskok, Narayana R. Aluru
prior_art_notes: Definitive treatment of gas and liquid flows from continuum to molecular regime, with emphasis on slip flow, Knudsen-number scaling, and DSMC/MD simulation methods for nanoscale transport. Anticipates: patents on gas-flow microsensors, slip-flow channels, Knudsen-pump devices, and molecular-scale nanofluidic transport — all reduce to textbook physics. Particularly load-bearing for nanofluidic-channel patents claiming non-continuum effects as novel.

canonical_name: Madou 2011 — Fundamentals of Microfabrication and Nanotechnology (3rd ed, 3-volume) (textbook)
creator: Marc J. Madou
prior_art_notes: Three-volume engineering reference covering MEMS and microfluidic fabrication: photolithography, soft-lithography, hot embossing, injection molding, LIGA, deep RIE, glass etching, bonding (anodic, fusion, thermocompression, plasma), and integration. Volume III specifically covers manufacturing techniques for microfluidics. Anticipates: any patent on a 'method of fabricating a microfluidic device' that claims a process step (lithography, etch, mold, bond) that is documented in Madou's textbook before the patent priority date. Standard examiner reference for fabrication 102/103 rejections.

canonical_name: Manz, Becker & Lee 1998 — Microsystem Technology in Chemistry and Life Sciences (textbook)
disclosure_citation: ISBN 978-3540655558; Springer Topics in Current Chemistry vol 194, 1998
creator: Andreas Manz, Holger Becker (eds.)
prior_art_notes: Edited Springer volume by the originators of µTAS/lab-on-a-chip; chapters cover microreaction technology, capillary electrophoresis chips, miniaturized analysis, and integrated bio-detection. By 1998 disclosure-genus, this volume time-stamps the integrated chemical-and-life-science 'lab on chip' platform concept in book-of-record form. Anticipates: any post-1998 patent claim to an 'integrated microsystem for chemical or biological analysis' as obvious; supplements the Manz 1990 Sensors and Actuators paper.
sources: Springer Topics in Current Chemistry vol 194

canonical_name: Burns, Mastrangelo et al. 1998 — An integrated nanoliter DNA analysis device
creator: Mark A. Burns, Brian N. Johnson, Sundaresh N. Brahmasandra, Kalyan Handique, James R. Webster, Madhavi Krishnan, Timothy S. Sammarco, Piu M. Man, Darren Jones, Dylan Heldsinger, Carlos H. Mastrangelo, David T. Burke
prior_art_notes: Landmark Science paper: first end-to-end integrated DNA analysis cartridge combining metering, mixing, thermal cycling (PCR), electrophoretic separation, and on-chip fluorescence detection in a single silicon-glass device with on-chip air-pressure pumping and thermo-pneumatic valving. By 1998 disclosure-genus, anticipates virtually every later sample-to-answer molecular diagnostic cartridge patent that claims 'integration of metering + amplification + separation + detection on a single substrate'. Defeats novelty for the architectural genus of POC molecular cartridges (BioFire, Cepheid GeneXpert, Abbott ID Now all descend from this disclosure).

canonical_name: Manz et al. 1992 — Planar chips technology for miniaturization of separation systems (first electrophoretic separation on chip)
creator: Andreas Manz, Daniel J. Harrison, Elisabeth Verpoorte, Carlo S. Effenhauser, Albert Paulus, Hans Lüdi, H. Michael Widmer
prior_art_notes: First demonstration of an electrophoretic separation performed on a planar microfabricated chip. Predates Harrison 1992/1993 Anal. Chem. coverage of capillary electrophoresis on chip. Anticipates: any patent claim to 'a microfluidic chip comprising microfabricated channels in a planar substrate for electrophoretic separation of analytes' filed after 1992. Foundational disclosure for the entire chip-CE industry.

canonical_name: Hagen 1839 — On the motion of water in narrow cylindrical tubes (Hagen-Poiseuille flow)
disclosure_citation: G. Hagen, 'Über die Bewegung des Wassers in engen cylindrischen Röhren', Poggendorffs Annalen der Physik und Chemie 46, 423-442 (1839)
creator: Gotthilf Heinrich Ludwig Hagen
prior_art_notes: First quantitative experimental description of laminar pressure-driven flow in narrow cylindrical tubes, predating Poiseuille's 1840 publication. Establishes the fourth-power dependence of volumetric flow on tube radius (Hagen-Poiseuille law). Foundational for ALL pressure-driven microfluidic theory: every channel-resistance calculation, every flow-controller specification, every droplet-generator design implicitly relies on this 1839 disclosure. Anticipates: any patent that recites 'flow rate determined by pressure drop and channel hydraulic resistance' as part of its operating principle — the relation is 187 years old.
sources: Poggendorffs Annalen der Physik und Chemie vol 46 (1839)

canonical_name: Poiseuille 1840 — Experimental research on the motion of liquids in tubes of very small diameter
disclosure_citation: J.L.M. Poiseuille, 'Recherches expérimentales sur le mouvement des liquides dans les tubes de très petits diamètres', Comptes Rendus 11, 961-967 and 1041-1048 (1840); full memoir Mém. Savants Étrang. 9, 433-543 (1846)
creator: Jean Léonard Marie Poiseuille
prior_art_notes: Independent and more rigorous experimental establishment of pressure-driven laminar flow in capillary tubes; Poiseuille's name attaches to the law (Hagen-Poiseuille). For microfluidics, Poiseuille is the canonical 19th-century experimentalist demonstrating that the same physical relation governs flow in tubes from millimeter to capillary scale. Anticipates: any patent claim to a microfluidic 'channel of small diameter exhibiting laminar flow with parabolic velocity profile' as the operative physics; the parabolic profile in capillaries was experimentally established 1840.

canonical_name: Stokes 1851 — On the effect of internal friction of fluids on the motion of pendulums (Stokes drag, low-Re flow)
disclosure_citation: G.G. Stokes, 'On the effect of the internal friction of fluids on the motion of pendulums', Trans. Camb. Phil. Soc. 9, 8-106 (1851)
creator: George Gabriel Stokes
prior_art_notes: Foundational analysis of viscous flow at low Reynolds number; derives the Stokes drag formula F=6πµaU on a sphere — the canonical scaling for micro-particle motion in microfluidic channels. Anticipates: any patent that recites Stokes-drag-based separation, particle settling, or microbead capture in microfluidic flow as its operative physics. Required prior art for any 'particle separation by drag balance' claim. Also foundational for cell-handling microfluidics where Stokes drag balances against electrophoretic, dielectrophoretic, acoustic, or magnetic forces.

canonical_name: Marangoni 1865 — On the expansion of a droplet of liquid floating on the surface of another liquid (surface-tension-driven flow)
disclosure_citation: C. Marangoni, 'Sull'espansione delle goccie d'un liquido galleggianti sulla superfície di altro liquido', Tipografia dei Fratelli Fusi, Pavia (1865); subsequent treatment Nuovo Cim. ser. 2, vol 5/6 (1871)
creator: Carlo Giuseppe Matteo Marangoni
prior_art_notes: First mathematical and experimental treatment of flows induced by surface-tension gradients (Marangoni effect / Marangoni convection). Foundational for: thermocapillary microfluidic actuation, surfactant-driven droplet motion, evaporation-driven assembly (coffee ring, tear-drop printing), and any droplet-microfluidic process where surfactants modulate interfacial flow. Anticipates: claims to 'thermocapillary microfluidic pump', 'surfactant-driven droplet steering', or 'Marangoni-driven micromixing' as their operating principle — physics is 161 years old.

canonical_name: Plateau 1873 — Statique expérimentale et théorique des liquides soumis aux seules forces moléculaires
disclosure_citation: J.A.F. Plateau, 'Statique expérimentale et théorique des liquides soumis aux seules forces moléculaires', Gauthier-Villars, Paris (2 vol., 1873)
creator: Joseph Antoine Ferdinand Plateau
prior_art_notes: Foundational treatise on capillarity, soap films, minimal surfaces, and droplet/jet stability. Establishes Plateau's laws (geometry of soap-film junctions and Plateau borders) and the Plateau-Rayleigh instability criterion for jets. Foundational for: any droplet-microfluidic process exploiting jet break-up (flow-focusing, T-junction, co-flow), interfacial geometry (Plateau borders in foams), and minimal-surface microfabrication. Anticipates: claims to droplet generators that recite jet-break-up as their operating principle; the criterion is 153 years old.

canonical_name: Rayleigh 1879 — On the instability of jets (Plateau-Rayleigh instability)
disclosure_citation: Lord Rayleigh, 'On the instability of jets', Proc. London Math. Soc. s1-10, 4-13 (1879); doi:10.1112/plms/s1-10.1.4
creator: John William Strutt, 3rd Baron Rayleigh
prior_art_notes: Quantitative linear-stability analysis showing that a cylindrical liquid jet is unstable to perturbations of wavelength greater than its circumference (most-unstable wavelength ≈ 9.02 r), leading to break-up into droplets. Anticipates: every droplet-microfluidic generator (T-junction, flow-focusing, co-flow), every continuous-inkjet printhead, every drop-on-demand piezo printhead, every microfluidic emulsion generator. The criterion is the operating physics of these devices and is 147 years old. Particularly load-bearing for inkjet/drop-generator patents claiming 'a method of producing droplets of controlled size by perturbing a liquid jet'.

canonical_name: Helmholtz 1858 — On integrals of the hydrodynamic equations corresponding to vortex motion
disclosure_citation: H. Helmholtz, 'Über Integrale der hydrodynamischen Gleichungen, welche den Wirbelbewegungen entsprechen', J. Reine Angew. Math. (Crelle) 55, 25-55 (1858)
creator: Hermann von Helmholtz
prior_art_notes: Foundational paper on vortex dynamics; establishes Helmholtz's vortex theorems. For microfluidics, foundational to: chaotic-advection mixers, secondary-flow effects in curved channels (Dean vortices), inertial microfluidics (Di Carlo), and any device exploiting vorticity for particle focusing or mixing. Anticipates: any patent claim that recites controlled vortex generation as its operating principle for mixing or focusing in micro-channels — the underlying vortex theorems are 168 years old.
sources: Crelle J. Reine Angew. Math. vol 55 (1858)

canonical_name: Maxwell 1867 — On the dynamical theory of gases (kinetic theory of viscosity)
disclosure_citation: J.C. Maxwell, 'On the dynamical theory of gases', Phil. Trans. Roy. Soc. London 157, 49-88 (1867)
creator: James Clerk Maxwell
prior_art_notes: Derivation of gas viscosity from kinetic theory; predicts viscosity is independent of pressure and proportional to sqrt(T). Foundational for: gas-flow microfluidics (gas chromatography on chip, micro gas sensors), Knudsen-number scaling at low pressure, and slip-flow corrections. Anticipates: claims that microscale gas-flow devices exhibit 'unexpected' viscosity behavior as novel — the kinetic-theory framework is 159 years old. Also load-bearing for any breath-analysis lab-on-chip claiming gas-phase transport effects.
sources: Phil. Trans. Roy. Soc. London vol 157 (1867)

canonical_name: Knudsen 1909 — The molecular current of gases through tubes (Knudsen number)
disclosure_citation: M. Knudsen, 'Die Gesetze der Molekularströmung und der inneren Reibungsströmung der Gase durch Röhren', Annalen der Physik 333(1), 75-130 (1909)
creator: Martin Knudsen
prior_art_notes: Foundational treatment of gas flow in narrow tubes when mean free path is comparable to channel width; introduces what becomes known as the Knudsen number Kn=λ/L and the slip/transition/free-molecular flow regimes. Anticipates: any nanofluidic or vacuum-microfluidic patent that claims operation in the slip or transition regime as novel — the regime classification is 117 years old. Particularly load-bearing for: Knudsen-pump devices, MEMS gas sensors, and nanopore gas-transport devices.

canonical_name: Reynolds 1886/1903 — Reynolds equation of lubrication theory (thin-film flow)
disclosure_citation: O. Reynolds, 'On the theory of lubrication and its application to Mr. Beauchamp Tower's experiments', Phil. Trans. Roy. Soc. London 177, 157-234 (1886); reprinted in O. Reynolds, Scientific Papers vol 2 (Cambridge Univ. Press, 1901)
creator: Osborne Reynolds
prior_art_notes: Foundational derivation of the Reynolds lubrication equation governing thin-film flow between nearly parallel surfaces. Foundational for: Hele-Shaw cell microfluidics, valve-membrane closure dynamics, squeeze-film damping in MEMS, and any microfluidic process where the flow occurs in a gap of small aspect ratio. Anticipates: claims to 'thin-film microfluidic device' or 'membrane valve with controlled closure dynamics' whose operating physics is the Reynolds equation — derivation is 140 years old.
sources: Phil. Trans. Roy. Soc. London vol 177 (1886)

canonical_name: Saffman & Taylor 1958 — The penetration of a fluid into a porous medium or Hele-Shaw cell containing a more viscous liquid (viscous fingering)
disclosure_citation: P.G. Saffman, G.I. Taylor, 'The penetration of a fluid into a porous medium or Hele-Shaw cell containing a more viscous liquid', Proc. Roy. Soc. A 245, 312-329 (1958); doi:10.1098/rspa.1958.0085
creator: Philip Geoffrey Saffman, Geoffrey Ingram Taylor
prior_art_notes: Foundational analysis of the interfacial instability when a less-viscous fluid displaces a more-viscous fluid in a Hele-Shaw cell or porous medium. Anticipates: microfluidic patents claiming 'controlled fingering for emulsion generation', 'pattern formation in microchannels', or 'porous-media-on-chip' devices — the underlying instability and its scaling are 68 years old. Critical reference for any displacement-flow microfluidic patent (chip-based EOR studies, blood-plasma separation by displacement, etc.).

canonical_name: Aris 1956 — On the dispersion of a solute in a fluid flowing through a tube (Aris extension to Taylor dispersion)
disclosure_citation: R. Aris, 'On the dispersion of a solute in a fluid flowing through a tube', Proc. Roy. Soc. A 235, 67-77 (1956); doi:10.1098/rspa.1956.0065
creator: Rutherford Aris
prior_art_notes: Aris's mathematical extension of Taylor's 1953 dispersion analysis to arbitrary cross-sections and to the asymptotic-time regime, giving the canonical 'Taylor-Aris dispersion coefficient' D_eff = D + Pe^2 D / 192 (for circular tube). Anticipates: any microfluidic patent that exploits or claims to mitigate hydrodynamic dispersion in a channel — the Taylor-Aris coefficient is the standard reference value, 70 years old. Critical to chip-CE, chip-HPLC, and any continuous-flow on-chip reactor where peak broadening matters.

canonical_name: Kelvin 1871 — Hydrokinetic solutions and observations (capillary waves and surface tension)
disclosure_citation: W. Thomson (Lord Kelvin), 'Hydrokinetic solutions and observations', Phil. Mag. ser. 4 vol 42, 362-377 (1871)
creator: William Thomson, 1st Baron Kelvin
prior_art_notes: Kelvin's analysis of capillary-gravity waves on liquid surfaces; establishes the dispersion relation for surface waves under combined surface-tension and gravity. Foundational for: any acoustofluidic device exploiting Faraday waves on a liquid film, capillary-wave-based atomization, or surface-acoustic-wave (SAW) liquid manipulation where capillary waves on the droplet surface participate. Anticipates: capillary-wave atomizer claims and surface-wave-driven micro-mixing claims — the dispersion relation is 155 years old.

canonical_name: Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics — microfluidics review series (Squires-Quake, Stone-Stroock-Ajdari, Di Carlo, Anna)
disclosure_citation: Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. — recurring microfluidics chapters: Stone, Stroock & Ajdari 36, 381 (2004) doi:10.1146/annurev.fluid.36.050802.122124; Squires & Quake (cross-listed Rev. Mod. Phys. 77, 977, 2005); Anna 48, 285 (2016) doi:10.1146/annurev-fluid-122414-034425; Di Carlo et al. 47, 67 (2015)

prior_art_notes: Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics has published recurring microfluidics review chapters since 2004 covering: engineering flows in small devices (Stone-Stroock-Ajdari 2004, already in corpus as stone-2004-engineering-flows-microfluidics — this entry serves as the umbrella for the SERIES), droplet flows (Anna 2016), inertial microfluidics (Di Carlo 2014), nonlinear electrokinetics (Bazant 2009). Anticipates as a series: any microfluidic patent whose operating physics is treated in one of these review chapters as obvious to one skilled in the art. Useful as a meta-citation for prior-art landscape construction.

canonical_name: Voldman 2006 — Electrical forces for microscale cell manipulation (Annual Reviews of Biomed Eng)
disclosure_citation: doi:10.1146/annurev.bioeng.8.061505.095739; Annu. Rev. Biomed. Eng. 8, 425-454 (2006)
creator: Joel Voldman
prior_art_notes: Annual Reviews chapter cataloguing electrical methods (DEP, EP, electroosmosis, electrowetting, electroporation) for cell manipulation in microfluidic devices. Anticipates: any single-cell platform patent that claims electrical force as its manipulation principle without further inventive distinction — the catalog of electrical-force modalities for cells was published in 2006. Particularly load-bearing for DEP-trap, EP-sorter, and EWOD-cell-handling claims.

canonical_name: Qin, Xia & Whitesides 2010 / Nature Reviews Materials 2017 — soft lithography 20-year retrospective
disclosure_citation: doi:10.1038/nprot.2009.234; Nat. Protoc. 5, 491-502 (2010); plus Nature Reviews Materials retrospective volume 2 (2017) doi:10.1038/natrevmats.2017.16 'Three decades of microfluidics'

Anticipates: any patent claiming a fabrication process consisting of 'replica-molding a PDMS device against a photolithographically defined master' as obvious in view of the reviewed methods. Standard examiner reference for soft-litho 102/103.

canonical_name: Lab on a Chip 2018 — 30 years of microfluidics special issue (editorial + retrospective)

Anticipates: any post-2018 patent claim that re-frames a previously published microfluidic concept (paper-based, droplet, organ-on-chip, dmf, etc.) as novel; the retrospective volume serves as a single-citation umbrella that an examiner can use to reject 'novel microfluidic platform' claims as obvious in view of the field history.

canonical_name: Jonathan Cooper et al. — Bioprocess engineering and microfluidic textbook tradition
disclosure_citation: J.M. Cooper (ed.), 'Bioprocess Engineering' and related Glasgow microfluidics texts (2002 onwards); ISBN 978-0470016213 (Wiley) for representative volume
creator: Jonathan M. Cooper (ed.)
prior_art_notes: Series of textbook chapters and edited volumes from the Glasgow bioengineering group covering microfluidic bioprocessing, biosensing, and integrated bioanalysis. Draft entry — exact ISBN/edition for the canonical volume needs verification before commons-grade promotion. Useful as a placeholder for the bioprocess-engineering textbook lineage that anchors microfluidic-bioprocess patents.

canonical_name: Wirth (ed.) 2013 — Microreactors in Organic Chemistry and Catalysis (Wiley) and Hessel et al. — Chemical Micro Process Engineering
disclosure_citation: T. Wirth (ed.), 'Microreactors in Organic Chemistry and Catalysis', 2nd ed., Wiley-VCH 2013, ISBN 978-3527332991; V. Hessel, S. Hardt, H. Löwe 'Chemical Micro Process Engineering' Wiley-VCH 2004, ISBN 978-3527308354
creator: Thomas Wirth (ed.); Volker Hessel et al.

Cover: micromixer designs (T, Y, multilamination, interdigital, split-and-recombine), residence-time engineering, heat-exchange in microreactors, scale-out vs scale-up, and catalytic micropacked beds. Anticipates: industrial-process patent claims to 'continuous-flow microreactor with high heat-transfer coefficient and short residence time' as obvious in view of the textbook tradition. canonical_name: Voldman et al. — Cells in microfluidics (microfluidic single-cell textbook tradition)
disclosure_citation: J. Voldman et al., MIT graduate-course materials and edited volumes on microfluidic cell handling; J. El-Ali, P.K. Sorger, K.F. Jensen 'Cells on chips' Nature 442, 403-411 (2006) doi:10.1038/nature05063 serves as the canonical citable companion review

prior_art_notes: MIT-anchored line of textbooks and reviews covering microfluidic single-cell handling: trapping (DEP, mechanical, hydrodynamic, optical), perfusion, stimulation, and analysis. The El-Ali Sorger Jensen 2006 Nature review serves as the canonical citable anchor. Anticipates: any patent claiming a microfluidic single-cell trap-and-analyze architecture (mechanical, hydrodynamic, DEP, optical) as obvious in view of the 2006 review and subsequent textbook coverage.

canonical_name: Annual Review of Biomedical Engineering — microfluidics series (Beebe 2002, Voldman 2006, Toner & Irimia 2005, Bhatia 2014)
disclosure_citation: Annu. Rev. Biomed. Eng. recurring microfluidics chapters: Beebe-Mensing-Walker 4, 261 (2002); Toner & Irimia 7, 77 (2005) doi:10.1146/annurev.bioeng.7.011205.135108; Voldman 8, 425 (2006); Bhatia & Ingber 16, 1 (2014); Sackmann 16, 17 (2014)
creator: David Beebe, Glennys Mensing, Glenn Walker, Mehmet Toner, Daniel Irimia, Joel Voldman, Sangeeta Bhatia, Donald Ingber, et al.

As a series, the chapters constitute a continuous published research-program record from 2002 onwards covering: physics of microfluidics, blood-on-chip, cell manipulation, organ-on-chip, biomedical applications. Anticipates: any patent in the biomedical microfluidics space claiming a method or device whose operating principle is reviewed in this series — useful for examiners constructing 102/103 rejections by single-source citation.

canonical_name: Stone, Stroock & Ajdari 2004 — Engineering flows in small devices (extended bibliographic anchor)
creator: Howard A. Stone, Abraham D. Stroock, Armand Ajdari
prior_art_notes: Companion citation to the existing stone-2004-engineering-flows-microfluidics entry — kept as a distinct slug to capture the full author trio (Stone, Stroock, Ajdari) and the explicit Annual Reviews of Fluid Mechanics framing as an engineering-design review covering chaotic mixing (herringbone), electrokinetic injection schemes, droplet generation, and induced-charge electrokinetics. canonical_name: Becker & Locascio 2002 — Polymer microfluidic devices (review)
creator: Holger Becker, Laurie E. Locascio
prior_art_notes: Foundational review of polymer (PMMA, PC, COC, PS, PDMS) microfluidic fabrication: hot embossing, injection molding, laser ablation, solvent bonding, thermal bonding. Anticipates: any patent on a 'thermoplastic microfluidic device fabricated by hot-embossing or injection-molding with thermal or solvent bonding' as obvious in view of this 2002 review. Critical reference for commercial cartridge IP landscape (BioFire, Cepheid, Abbott ID Now, etc. all use thermoplastic processes documented here).

canonical_name: Salimetrics SalivaBio Oral Swab (SOS)
disclosure_citation: Salimetrics LLC product datasheet, SalivaBio Oral Swab (SOS) Item 5001.06 (2009); company website salimetrics.com
creator: Salimetrics LLC
channel_geometry: absorbent inert synthetic polymer cylinder ~30 mm × 8 mm; centrifuge-recoverable saliva volume up to 1.5 mL
sample_volume: 0.5 to 1.5 mL saliva
sensing: off-chip immunoassay (cortisol, DHEA, testosterone, alpha-amylase, sIgA)
notable_capabilities: compatible with all Salimetrics salivary cortisol immunoassays

prior_art_notes: Discloses an inert absorbent collection wand whose synthetic polymer composition is specifically certified non-interfering with downstream cortisol, sex-steroid, and alpha-amylase immunoassays — a non-trivial materials-engineering disclosure because cotton (the historic Salivette material) measurably absorbs steroids. Anticipates: collection consumables claiming validated zero-bias for salivary steroid panels; pediatric variants of oral fluid wands sized for sub-6-year-old donors; centrifuge-recovery workflow producing a defined minimum saliva volume from passive-drool sampling. The swab is the upstream element of nearly every academic salivary biomarker microfluidic assay published 2010 onward, and is functionally a pre-concentrator/sample-prep consumable for downstream lab-on-chip cortisol cartridges.
sources: Salimetrics SalivaBio Oral Swab product page and IFU
Granger DA et al., Psychoneuroendocrinology 2007 — comparison of saliva collection materials
notes: Bridge consumable: non-microfluidic itself, but it is the validated inlet for essentially every saliva-based microfluidic diagnostic chip in academic literature. Included to anchor that lineage.

canonical_name: DNA Genotek Oragene•DNA OG-500 Saliva Collection Kit

creator: DNA Genotek Inc. (subsequently OraSure Technologies)

The architecture is a single-use, single-action lysis-and-mix cartridge that anticipates: any consumer mail-back DNA kit using a sealed reagent lid that releases on close; passive volumetric mixing of donor sample with preservation reagent without active pumping; room-temperature ambient-shipping nucleic-acid stabilization workflows. The OG-500 variant specifically is the kit shipped by 23andMe and AncestryDNA from 2008 onward and is the most widely-deployed microfluidic-grade sample-prep cartridge in human history (>30 million units shipped).
sources: DNA Genotek Oragene•DNA OG-500 datasheet PD-PR-006
US8221381B2 (saliva collection device with mechanism for releasing stabilizing reagent)

notes: Distinct from existing 23andme-saliva-collection-tube and ancestry-saliva-collection-kit entries which describe the consumer-branded products. This entry covers the underlying DNA Genotek OEM cartridge.

prior_art_notes: Discloses a chamber-free 'crystal' digital PCR architecture in which an aqueous sample is partitioned into a 2D monolayer of monodisperse droplets confined between two parallel surfaces inside a microfluidic chip. The chip integrates a flow-focusing droplet generator with an immobilization chamber whose gap height is matched to droplet diameter so that droplets self-organize into a hexagonally close-packed 2D crystal. Anticipates: (a) any digital PCR architecture relying on geometrically constrained 2D droplet arrays for thermal cycling and image-based digital readout; (b) integrated single-chip dPCR cartridges with on-chip droplet generation, thermal cycling, and multi-color fluorescence imaging without an external droplet reader; (c) the use of close-packing density rather than addressed wells for partitioning. Material relevant to claims of Bio-Rad QX-series patents asserting required chambered/well architectures.
sources: Madic et al. 'Three-color crystal digital PCR' Biomol Detect Quantif 2016 doi:10.1016/j.bdq.2016.10.002
